QUESTION OF THE WEEK - The prospect of a fifth interest rate cut has been firmly put on the agenda since the release of surprisingly weak May labour force data.
Economists were surveyed on their outlook for interest rates and the labour market.
While employment growth is expected to be positive over the second half of the year, most see it moving at a pace that is consistent only with flat, or slightly improving unemployment.

While some of the weakness of the labour force data has been seen as reflecting its status of lagging indicator, economists said the fact that growth more generally appeared to have stalled after a strong start to 1997 meant ongoing jobs weakness would affect confidence and therefore prospects for recovery.
Given that jobs are also a major concern of voters, economists said the prospect of high unemployment would increase the pressure for a rate cut.

The run of weak data, including the jobs figures, since the May 23 interest rate cut has seen economists lift the possibility of there being a fifth rate cut, which is now seen as a better than even chance. ----------------------------------------------------------------

DWELLING UNIT COMMENCEMENTS - Housing starts are expected to post their second successive quarterly rise in the March quarter, reflecting the signs of an improving housing sector seen so far. Housing looks like being one of the strongest areas of the economy in 1997, and building and finance approvals data suggests it got off to a good start to the year, economists said.
